a:r.a:t: We always keep our confidential files at a safe place so that no one is able to access them or tamper with them. In the same way, the computer too can help you to protect your confidential files from unwanted access. You can protect confidential files by rendering them some attributes such as Read Only, Archive and Hidden.
If you set the Read Only attribute for a file, the other users will only be able to read that file but cannot modify or delete it.
If you set the Archive attribute for a file, it means you have not taken the backup of that file.
If you set the Hidden attribute for a file, it becomes invisible so that no one else can see it.
(In case you want to view the hidden files, you will need to follow the following steps:
- Click on Tools menu in the Windows Explorer
- From the drop down menu select 'Folders Options' Option
- Click on the 'Show all files' option)
For setting these attributes, right-click on the file and select Properties option. In the Properties dialog box, you can set any or all of the attributes described above.
This handouts gives you an idea on how to secure files on your system by giving them some attributes such as making them hidden and protecting them from being tampered.

It is a common practice to keep more than one copy of important and crucial documents. Similarly you also need to have more than one copy of your important files on your computer. Keeping a file in more than one place helps you in protecting the file in case it gets corrupted.
You can also make a copy of your file in case you need it for some other purposes.
The copy of a file can be made by using the copy command of Windows. For this, select copy option from the edit menu or by right-click on the file and select the copy option from the shortcut menu.
This handouts teaches you how to locate a file and copy it to a different location with a different name.

You may also need to protect your files and folders over the network so as to prevent unauthorized access. For the folders that you do not want to share or make available to others, simply apply the 'Not Shared' attribute. For the folders you want to share, you can assign different levels of sharing for different users over the network by applying 'Read Only' or 'Full' attributes.
In case of 'Read Only' access, users over the network can only view your file or folder but cannot perform any file-related activities.
In case of Full access, you enable other users to access, modify and delete the folder or file.

For setting these attributes, right-click on the file and select the Properties option. In the Properties dialog-box, select the Sharing tab. In the sharing dialog-box, you can set any of the attributes described above. You can also assign a different password for each type of permission.
This handouts gives you an idea on how to secure files over the network by giving them some attributes, and thus protecting them from being tampered.

At your home or at the office, you arrange your files in filing cabinets. Windows also allows you to create folders, which are equivalent to a filing cabinet. Within these folders you can store your documents or files. Thus a folder is a way of organizing the files at one place. Files related to one work or task can be stored in one folder. Just as a filing cabinet is considered to be a folder, its section, which contains various types of files can be called sub-folders. On computers you can organize your data in various sub-folders, which can be a part of a big folder.

Now, when you arrange data in various folders, it becomes essential that you name or rename the folders. Creating and renaming folders is a very simple process. For creating a folder, you should move to the location where you want to create a new folder. If you want your folder to be contained inside another folder just open that folder and create your folder inside that folder.

You can create folders in the following ways. You may either select the 'New' option from the 'File' menu or just select 'New' option from the popup menu, which appears by right-clicking inside the main folder.

You can also give folders meaningful names so that you get a hint on their content. For renaming a folder just right-click on the folder you want to rename and select rename option from the popup menu that appears.

Windows offers you a quick way of launching a program or opening a folder without having to go through the entire process of opening start menu or through windows explorer.

You can create desktop shortcuts for most frequently used programs or folders. After creating desktop shortcuts, you can simply double-click the icons to open them. To create Desktop shortcuts, right click the mouse on the desktop or press the keyboard shortcut key and then select New->Shortcut options respectively.

Locate the program or folder for which a shortcut is to be created. For this click on the browse button or simply specify the path of the program or the folder in the Create Shortcuts dialog box. Specify a name for it and windows will create a shortcut (icon) for that program on the desktop.

- Tile Windows Horizontally: Windows are arranged one below the other.
- Tile Windows Vertically: Windows are arranged side by side.

Windows also provides you with three buttons on top of each window. The three buttons are minimize, maximize/restore and close buttons, placed in the same order.

Misplacing or loosing files in offices is a common incident. Often we have to waste a lot of time in tracing them. Such a situation can be easily averted with the help of computers.
In Windows, the find command will help you to locate files on your computer quickly and easily. For finding files or folders you need to specify any one of the following information:
- File name or a part of it
- The date the file was created modified or saved

Windows also provides the feature of deleting unwanted files. The files you do not need can be conveniently deleted using the delete command. To delete a file, select the delete command from the edit menu or select it from the popup menu which appears when you right-click on that particular file.

When you delete a file, Windows stores that file in a folder named Recycle Bin. In case you delete a file accidentally, you can always get it back to its original location by restoring it from the Recycle Bin. In case you do not need the file any more, you can permanently delete that file by deleting it from the Recycle Bin. For deleting the file from the Recycle Bin double-click on the Recycle Bin icon on the desktop, select the file that you want to delete permanently and select the Empty Recycle Bin button.
This handouts shows how to search for files on your system and delete the unwanted files. It also shows how to permanently delete a file from the hard disk through the Recycle bin.

Any sort of work that you do on papers can be done more easily on a computer. For example, you can write letters or memos in Notepad or Wordpad applications. You can also create graphic files, database files etc. As a company maintains a register for keeping the details of its employees, a computer stores these details in its database. You can store your files on the computer by saving them. Saving of files means writing the files on the computers hard disk so that you can retrieve them later to work on them again.

You can create any kind of file by opening the appropriate application from the start menu or by double-clicking on the shortcut for that application present on the desktop. After working on the file, you can save it by any one of the following:
- Selecting Save option from the File menu;
- Selecting Save option which appears when you right-click on that particular file; or
- Windows will automatically ask for saving the file when you close the file.
This handouts tells you how to open an application like Notepad, type on it and save it on the computer's hard disk.

Windows Explorer is a tool that enables you to perform file related activities such as copy, move or delete files quickly and easily. It is a tool to browse through the entire system including the network. You can also see the various drives such as floppy drive, CD drive and the hard disk drive in the All Folders window. These drives are used to save files and folders. If you want to see the folders on any one of the drives you have to click on the '+' sign of that particular drive. This will enable you to view all the contents of the various drives and folders or files contained in Windows Explorer.
You can open Windows Explorer by right-clicking on the start menu and selecting the Explorer option or by selecting the Windows Explorer option from the Programs menu.
